title: Particle-Guided Diffusion Models for Partial Differential Equations
claim: Our method is evaluated on diverse PDE systems, each with a coefficient field and solution field observed only at sparse pixels.
layout: 2x5 grid of heatmaps, columns per PDE, top coefficient, bottom solution
description: A two-row, five-column grid of contour heatmaps, one column per PDE system: Darcy, Helmholtz, NS bounded, NS nonbounded and Poisson. The top row shows the coefficient field (labeled a) and the bottom row shows the solution field (labeled u). Fields use a diverging blue-to-red colormap, with a grayish tint in the mid-range. Black or colored square dots are scattered over each panel and mark the known observed pixels. Darcy's coefficient field is a piecewise two-region red and blue map. The NS bounded panels show a circular obstacle with a flow wake. A small legend box at the bottom center reads 'Known pixels' beside a black square. The eye goes first to the saturated Darcy panel at top left.
caption: Contour plot of the ground truth parameters overlayed with the observed values (highlighted pixels) for each PDE. The top row shows the coefficient field and the bottom row shows the solution field.
abstract: We introduce a guided stochastic sampling method that augments sampling from diffusion models with physics-based guidance derived from partial differential equation (PDE) residuals and observational constraints, ensuring generated samples remain physically admissible. We embed this sampling procedure within a new Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) framework, yielding a scalable generative PDE solver. Across multiple benchmark PDE systems as well as multiphysics and interacting PDE systems, our method produces solution fields with lower numerical error than existing state-of-the-art generative methods.
